I maintain a fleet of 40 FDE'd chromebooks running gentoo hardened (with libressl and musl). Quickpkg makes it so I can deploy a new asset in less than 5 minutes from netboot. All my servers are running the same base distro, with a different packagelist. Because I run my company, I get to make those decisions. Because it's so brain-dead easy to keep updated/maintained, I dedicate maybe an hour per week making sure all the users are okay. Apps like OCS Inventory NG help greatly with this task. I know of three or four large enterprise gentoo installs, outside of google's projects, and they were all chosen because five-nines (99.999%) stability was the main requirement.

The benefit is, if you know what you're doing, you don't need an entire IT team to run shit. It should all be handled by very small shell scripts anyway. I've personally performed (Ubuntu) linux enterprise conversions where we ended up giving half the team severance packages because they weren't needed to babysit the servers anymore.
